summary: Install-time beacon exfiltrates host identity to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: react-bootstrap-table-next-bg is a typosquat of react-bootstrap-table-next. Its package.json wires both preinstall and postinstall lifecycle hooks to beacon.js, which on every npm install collects hostname, username, current working directory, platform, INIT_CWD, npm_package_name, and the npm user agent, and sends them via plain HTTP GET to the hardcoded bare-IP collector http://100.24.177.136/cb/c469e93cbb94/depconf/react-bootstrap-table-next-bg. The destination is an unauthenticated IP endpoint unrelated to any legitimate publisher, the transport is cleartext, and the behavior fires automatically on default install without consent. The package self-labels as a 'dependency-confusion PoC', but that label is author-controlled and does not consent for arbitrary installers (including internal builds reached via name confusion) whose host identity and workspace path are shipped to the operator of the bare-IP collector.
